The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: The outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card started rejecting those requests, and the shop's account pages failed every time that request failed.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 6m 53s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 100.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 14,635.76 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for - not taken

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 19:13 UTC, not back to normal by 19:19:53 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 4 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 19:30:48 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 19:19:28 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 19:19:53 UTC - no code fix looked for

Summary
The service broke at 19:13 UTC and was not back to normal by 19:19:53 UTC, at least 6 minutes 53 seconds later. 97.4% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 100.0% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 14,635.76 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. The outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card started rejecting those requests, and the shop's account pages failed every time that request failed. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it. Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps rejecting the card lookup, and could fail the same way the next time io-pay has trouble.

Impact
at least 6m 53s - since onset, still not back to normal
100.0% - peak error rate
8,178 - requests failed
0.9% to 97.4% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 14,635.76 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Account page requests in io-shop call the card lookup of io-pay, a payment provider run by IO Payments Ltd. From the onset io-pay answered that lookup with 503, and io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed and failed the whole account page request.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages failed to load. io-shop's own log reported that the account page error rate was at its worst, and from the onset account page requests failed.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 31 occurrences in 37 minutes, 18:43–19:19; # was 0.50% to 100.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:14
    Gbf7d ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:13–19:19; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card took 14 different values
    T5 19:19:44 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 19:13
why 1 Account page requests failed because the card lookup that io-shop makes to the third-party payment provider io-pay returned 503. io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 and failed the request.
  Evidence:
    Gbf7d
    T9 19:19:46 Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 19:14; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes.
      T7
      T8
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 19:19:48.
      T14
why 2 io-pay, which IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning 503 on the card lookup at the onset. The record does not show why: io-pay's own state was not read, only io-shop's logs of its replies.
  Evidence:
    Gbf7d
    T9
Contributing factors
- When io-pay's card lookup failed, io-shop failed the whole account page request. No fallback was seen, such as rendering the page without the card details or using a cached copy. (AI-2, AI-3)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | From 19:13 UTC the third-party payment provider io-pay (api.io-pay.example, owned by IO Payments Ltd) began returning 503s on the card lookup. Every account page render calls it, so the error rate went to 100% and latency rose to about 2s. No deploy, flag or rollout change on io-shop, and cpu and memory were flat. | 0.93 | never tried: the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 19:19:52 | Refused to act on C1 - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 19:13 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 19:19:04 UTC, 6 minutes 4 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay (api.io-pay.example) and to say why it failed | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Make the io-shop account page render without card details, instead of failing the request, when io-pay's card lookup returns an error. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Add a test that the account page still renders when io-pay's card lookup returns 503. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 40 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 19:13.
- 44 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 44 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 19:19:48.
- 48 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for.
- 49 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus moved the incident to ESCALATED - no code fix looked for.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

T10 | 19:19:46 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 minutes 4 seconds before 19:19:04

Response effort
none - engineer time
88,071 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/0c3876a2-dc34-4589-9ea6-7c2164bb5461
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 43 occurrences in 29 minutes, 18:43–19:11
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 31 occurrences in 37 minutes, 18:43–19:19; # was 0.50% to 100.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:14
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 6 occurrences in 29 minutes, 18:44–19:12
Gbf7d | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:13–19:19; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card took 14 different values
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed to load for shoppers whose page asked for their saved card. This lasted at least {duration}. The cause was IO Payments Ltd, the outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card. It started rejecting those requests, and every time a request failed, the account page failed too. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates that this cost the shop at least {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody on call was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus took no action to end it, because the failure is in a service another company runs and nothing Argus can do reaches it. Its recommended step is to ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is being looked for. That step has not been taken.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
